summary: Aermotor tower built near Pembine, Wisconsin, in 1933 or 1934; surplused and sold 1990, moved to Paust's resort 1991, now in Governor Thompson State Park; NHLR-registered 2003.

facts.design: 100-foot Aermotor tower (NHLR); the Historical Society record lists its wall material as metal and names International Stacey Company in the architect field

staffing.status: Active lookout until the 1980s (Historical Society and Register); no staffing names found in the sources read

access.note: The Register lists the location as Governor Thompson State Park; no source says whether the tower itself can be climbed

events.note: Built at its original location in November 1933 (Wisconsin Historical Society); the Register gives 1934 and credits the CCC
A November 1936 newspaper item, quoted on the Faithorn lookout page (Michigan), mentions the Wisconsin fire tower near Pembine as a telephone link point
State declared the tower surplus and sold it to Dale Paust
Moved by Dale Paust to his Woods Lake resort, its current location (Historical Society); the Register says he moved and rebuilt it there without a date
State purchased the resort for a state park; Governor Thompson State Park was created (Register, Wikipedia)

corrections.why: The 'None relocated' label contradicts the note that the tower was moved, and the record omits the 1991 move.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Historical Society record gives November 1933 at the original location and does not mention the CCC; the Register gives 1934 and says the CCC built it. Both are recorded. The story notes the one-year gap and that only the Register names the CCC.
The Register calls it an Aermotor tower; the Historical Society record names International Stacey Company in its architect field. Not reconciled; both are recorded.

notes_for_editor: Few sources. No staffing names or specific fires were found for the Pembine tower. The Register and the Historical Society agree on the 1990 sale and the 1980s service end, and disagree on the build year by one year. Wikipedia is a lead only; its park facts are stated as Wikipedia's. Whether the tower can be climbed is not stated anywhere; the story tells readers to ask the park. A Geocaching page repeats the Register's text and was not used as a source.
